speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in view of the ongoing situation and the progress of implementing the "Five-Point Consensus" in Myanmar, what is the Ministry's assessment of the impact on ASEAN's unity and image.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I would emphasise that the key word is "consistency" and ASEAN, under the Chairmanship of Laos, has expressed our clear intention to maintain that consistent position, and the paramount expression of that is the Five-Point Consensus.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I would say that, as far as ASEAN is concerned, there is no change.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The unfortunate change, which is happening, is on the ground in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst the military has no intention of ceding power, their ability to maintain authority on the ground is being severely challenged by a variety of groups, both the ethnic armed organisations as well as the resistance from the Burmese majority within Myanmar itself.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our priority remains the welfare of the people of Myanmar and we should be under no illusions that ASEAN can magically resolve the problems.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ultimately, this is a political problem, a problem of leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, it is a complex situation, but we will continue to maintain our consistent position.
